title: Profile compatibility shim and backcompat bridge for verified performance profiles
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: As we expand the set of Redwood-verified performance profiles, breaking changes (field additions, renames, or stricter cost normalization logic) can cause downstream regressions for customers who pin older model versions or for runtime components that expect a stable profile schema. This ticket defines a compatibility shim and back-compatibility bridge to ensure older clients and runtime consumers can continue to operate while we evolve profile metadata and cost-normalization algorithms.

Goals:
- Provide a server-side compatibility layer that can polyfill or translate newer profile fields into legacy shapes on demand.
- Define a deterministic versioning and deprecation signal baked into the profile manifest (human- and machine-readable).
- Create deterministic translation rules for common schema changes (unit rename, latency field split, quantization tags).
- Automate canary verification to ensure translated profiles meet latency/throughput expectations within an acceptable delta before publishing translations to prod.

Context:
- This intersects with the verified profile publish pipeline, the runtime kernel-selection mapping, and Dedicated/Dedicated->Private routing logic. The compatibility bridge is intended as a short-to-medium term mitigation to reduce customer-impact while we converge on stable profile contracts.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a profile manifest version header (manifest_version) and a "translation_policy" tag for each published profile.
2) Implement a lightweight server-side translator service (profiles-compat) that accepts a requested compatibility target (e.g., legacy_v1) and emits a translated profile JSON.
3) Ship a canonical set of translation rules in a git-backed repo so translations are reviewable and auditable.
4) Extend the publish pipeline to generate and smoke-test translations during staging: a) generate translated profile, b) run a set of synthetic requests using the runtime harness, c) compare key metrics (p95 latency, tokens/sec, normalized cost) against an acceptance window.
5) Add a runtime flag that allows routing requests to the translated profile when a customer pin targets an older contract.

Implementation notes: translations should be idempotent, reversible when possible, and produce warnings in the profile metadata when lossy conversions occur.
acceptance_criteria: Profiles published with manifest_version include translation_policy or explicit deprecation metadata.
profiles-compat service can translate at least three common schema deltas (field rename, metric split, unit change) and return machine-validated JSON.
Publish pipeline runs smoke tests for translations and blocks publishing if translated p95 latency deviates >20% or normalized cost >15% compared to the source profile.
Runtime routing honor compatibility target headers for pinned model/version combinations without requiring customer-side changes.
Documentation and migration guide published in the profile docs and linked from Console onboarding flows.
Telemetry shows translation usage and a per-translation failure rate <2% after rollout.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging, 2 weeks): implement translation rules repo, basic profiles-compat service, and augment publish pipeline to emit translations into staging. Phase 2 (canary, 1 week): run smoke tests and enable translated profiles for 5 internal customers and default routes for staging runtime. Phase 3 (prod gated rollout, 2 weeks): enable translation for pinned requests with opt-in developer flag; monitor telemetry for regressions. Phase 4 (deprecation enforcement, 3 months): begin emitting deprecation warnings to customers and encourage repinning to newest manifest_version; iterate translation rule coverage. Rollback: disable routing flag and revert publish pipeline change if smoke tests fail or production translation error rate >5%.
telemetry_requirements: Emit the following metrics with profile translation label: translation_requests_total, translation_errors_total, translation_p95_latency_ratio, translation_cost_ratio_vs_source, translation_smoke_test_pass_rate. Log translation rule id, source_manifest_version, target_manifest_version, and any lossy_conversion flag. Surface aggregated telemetry on Console per-profile page and in runtime incident alerts.
risks_mitigation:
Risk: Translations produce semantics drift causing subtle quality regressions. Mitigation: impose conservative acceptance windows, require manual sign-off for translations that touch generation-control fields, and add golden-sample regression checks.
Risk: Operational complexity increases. Mitigation: keep translator lightweight and stateless, back translations into git for transparency, and instrument exhaustive test coverage for common transforms.
Risk: Performance overhead for runtime translation. Mitigation: cache translated artifacts, pre-generate translations in publish pipeline, and use CDN for distribution to runtimes.
